correctness.rationale: For a cellular embedding, locality after deleting \(A\) is equivalent to vanishing of the restricted nonzero ambient class in \(H^1(\mathbb{RP}^2;\mathbb F_2)\). This is equivalent to a vertex cochain \(f\) with \(u=\delta f\) on every surviving edge, so \(\alpha(G)\) is the minimum support of \(u+\delta f\). That is exactly signed-graph frustration. Cellular Poincare duality preserves support cardinality and converts those cocycles to dual \(1\)-cycles in the nonzero homology class. The double-cover formula follows from the lift criterion for the generator. All quantifiers and the cellularity boundary are explicit.

value.rationale: The identity gives a geometric and algorithmic interpretation of a newly introduced knot-theoretic graph invariant. In cellular projective-plane embeddings the generic edge-deletion optimization becomes an exact shortest nontrivial dual-cycle problem, equivalently an antipodal shortest-path problem in the spherical double cover. Substituting this into the source theorem converts Jones-piece breadth deficits into dual systoles. This is a structural bridge with reusable computational and conceptual value, not a low-parameter recomputation.
